clue.text: Unfriendly? Get shot

parts.note: to get a prize is to win it
a shot at something is a try

explanation.surface: A curt question about hostility, followed by a brusque suggestion to go and get a photo taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A wintry manner is cold and cheerless, so figuratively unfriendly.

clue.text: People like us grow up being transformable

parts.note: people like us are 'we'

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word for grow is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to flower is to grow and bloom

explanation.surface: Someone muses that people like them grow up able to change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People like us' is the subject in the surface but gives the pronoun; 'grow' must be read as the verb to bloom, and 'up' turns it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who turns into a wolf is a creature able to change its shape, a transformable being.

clue.text: More pleasant resort on river

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A holiday spot by the water is judged more agreeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicer is the comparative of nice, a plain synonym for more pleasant.

clue.text: Old railwaymen turned up in sequence

indicators.note: in a down clue 'turned up' means the union's letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, a former British trade union

explanation.surface: Retired railway workers appear one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses NUR, the old National Union of Railwaymen, a British trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A run is an unbroken series, as in a run of wins, so a sequence.

clue.text: In pain? Diagnose problem

indicators.note: a problem with the word diagnose is that its letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor asks whether the patient is hurting and then tries to identify the trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Agonised means suffering great anguish, so in pain.

clue.text: Astronomer, a female one, attached to constellation

parts.note: a gal is an informal word for a girl or woman
I is the Roman numeral for one
Leo is the constellation of the lion

explanation.surface: A woman stargazer is linked with a particular group of stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo Galilei was the Italian scientist who pioneered telescope observation of the heavens.

clue.text: Indistinguishable changes made in second print

indicators.note: changes made to the words second print rearrange their letters

explanation.surface: A reprint revised in its second run looks just like the first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made in' is a link joining the anagram signal 'changes' to its fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nondescript lacks distinctive features, so it cannot easily be told apart.

clue.text: Parasite Uriah has to stay around

indicators.note: the word for stay goes around the surname of Dickens's Uriah

parts.note: to stick somewhere is to stay there
Uriah Heep is the fawning clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield

explanation.surface: A bloodsucker called Uriah has to remain in the vicinity.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep is the creeping, fawning clerk in Dickens's novel David Copperfield, so his name serves here.
explanation.definitionFit: The sheep tick is a bloodsucking mite or fly that lives on sheep, a parasite.

clue.text: River needing swan to make room for more water

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A river needs a swan to clear space for extra water.
explanation.definitionFit: To deepen a channel is to dig it further down so that it holds a greater volume.

clue.text: Commit murder in field

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Commit murder in field', gives DO for 'Commit' but no word yields MAIN or MA+IN; probably garbled in OCR and no source found

clue.text: Dancing bird, rook, invading hill

parts.note: the roc is the giant bird of Arabian legend

indicators.note: the chess piece's letter invades the word for hill, ending up inside it

parts.note: a knoll is a small hill
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A bird and a rook dance about while overrunning a hillock.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird here is the giant roc of Arabian legend; 'invading' signals the chess letter getting inside the hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock and roll is a lively style of popular music and the dancing done to it.

clue.text: Relation not inheriting estate, cousin excluded from the start

indicators.note: from the start of each of the five words that follow, only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A family member is cut out of an estate, while a cousin is shut out from the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a will dispute; in fact the initials of 'not inheriting estate, cousin excluded' spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sister's or brother's daughter, a family relative.

clue.text: Wandering amid flowers, I don't know what to say

definitions.text: I don't know what to say

indicators.note: wandering letters of amid flowers stray from their order into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone strolling among blooms is left speechless by their beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses being so moved or shocked that one is unable to speak.

clue.text: I went to the fair with the medicines I am taking

parts.note: simples are old herbal medicines made from a single plant
I'M ON is a way of saying I am taking a drug, as in 'I'm on antibiotics'

explanation.surface: A patient says they went to the fair carrying the drugs they are on.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme runs 'Simple Simon met a pieman going to the fair', so he speaks the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme the simpleton character meets a pieman while on his way to the fair.

clue.text: Anna's constituent for pastry dish

definitions.meaning: a small Indian coin, twelve of which made up one anna
a baked dish of filling in a pastry case

explanation.walkthrough: Anna is not a woman's name: the anna was a coin of British India, worth twelve of the smaller coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a tiny Indian coin, a fraction of the anna, and a baked pastry dish.

clue.text: Lover embracing popular rail worker

indicators.note: the word for lover embraces, holding inside it, the word for popular

parts.note: leman is an old word for a lover or sweetheart
IN means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A sweetheart cuddles a well-liked railway employee.
explanation.walkthrough: LEMAN, an archaic word for a lover, embraces IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A lineman is someone who lays or maintains railway track, a worker on the line.

clue.text: Be near rough, be in trouble

indicators.note: trouble stirs up the letters of rough, be in into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to stay close to the rough on the golf course and land in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' reads as a phrase, but 'in' is part of the fodder and 'trouble' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To neighbour something is to adjoin it or lie close beside it, the verb sense.

clue.text: Mythical creature took refuge in lady's slipper, perhaps

parts.note: an orc is a monster of folklore and fantasy
to hide is to take refuge, so took refuge is hid

explanation.surface: A fabled monster shelters inside a woman's shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: The lady's slipper is a wild flower, not footwear; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The lady's slipper is a type of wild orchid with a pouch-shaped flower.

clue.text: This should get filled with fish caught in a group

definitions.text: This should get filled with fish

indicators.note: the word for caught sits in the word for a group

parts.note: a set is a group of things
taken can mean caught or captured

explanation.surface: A container meant to be filled with the fish a group has caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake net is a fishing net hung on stakes, designed to fill with fish.

clue.text: Get a boost from drug, provided it's about

indicators.note: about here turns the pair of words round so they are read backwards

parts.note: a pill is a dose of medicine or a drug
if means provided, as in on condition that

explanation.surface: Someone takes a drug for a lift, as long as it is around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses PILL + IF as a whole, giving FILLIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a stimulus or encouragement, something that gives a boost.

clue.text: Rustic bird Henry ditched

indicators.note: the letter for Henry is ditched, thrown out of the word for bird

parts.note: the pheasant is a game bird
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A country bird is abandoned by someone called Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry is not a man: the henry is the unit of electrical inductance, symbol H.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a country labourer, so a rustic used as a noun.

clue.text: Sport a jumper

definitions.meaning: a bat-and-ball team game played chiefly in Britain and the Commonwealth
an insect related to the grasshopper that leaps and chirps

explanation.surface: Someone is told to wear a sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a jumper' looks like the British word for a sweater, but here it is a leaping insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a bat-and-ball game and a chirping leaping insect.

clue.text: Trust councillor to make changes

parts.note: Cllr or Cr is an abbreviation for councillor
to edit is to make changes to a text

explanation.surface: A council member is trusted to revise something.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit means belief or faith placed in someone, as in giving credit to a story.

clue.text: Author said to demand an extortionate price

indicators.note: said means the author's surname is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: Arthur Ransome was the English author of Swallows and Amazons

explanation.surface: A writer is reported to be charging outrageous sums.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur RANSOME, author of Swallows and Amazons, sounds the same once the final E is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransom a captive is to demand a large payment for their release.

clue.text: End of fire is no less hot

parts.note: as can mean equally or no less, as in 'as hot'
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A fire's dying embers are said to be every bit as hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is the powdery residue left when a fire burns out.

clue.text: Wanting to be an actor, organises relations

parts.note: to stage an event is to organise it
truck means dealings or relations, as in 'have no truck with'

explanation.surface: A would-be performer sets up family gatherings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relations' is not family: TRUCK means dealings, as in having no truck with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage-struck describes someone captivated by the theatre and longing to perform.

clue.text: Swelling reduced as bachelor leaves for wedding

indicators.note: the bachelor's letter leaves the word for swelling, going out of it

parts.note: a bunion is a painful swelling on the foot
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA

explanation.surface: A foot ailment eases as a single man departs for his marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced as' and 'for' are link words; 'leaves' signals that B is removed from BUNION.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a marriage, the joining of two people at a wedding.

clue.text: Altering end of tale brings violent reaction

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Altering end of tale brings violent reaction', suggests STORY with its end changed, but no clue word supplies the M; possibly garbled and no source found
annotationWithheld.clue: Altering end of tale brings violent reaction

clue.text: Being full of energy, I am entered in a race

indicators.note: the contraction is entered in the words for a race, placed inside them

parts.note: a nation is a race or people
I'M is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: Someone full of life says they have signed up for a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation means liveliness or vigour, the state of being full of energy.

clue.text: Some part of Germany

indicators.note: part of the country's name holds the letters, which run inside it

explanation.surface: A region within Germany is pointed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Any can mean some, as in 'is there any milk?'

clue.text: Friend outside teeming rain is to soak

indicators.note: the word for friend goes outside the jumbled rain

parts.note: a mate is a friend

indicators.note: teeming suggests rain churning, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A friend stands out in a downpour and gets soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teeming' reads as heavy rain falling but is the anagram signal; 'outside' puts the friend round the jumbled letters RINA.
explanation.definitionFit: To marinate food is to steep or soak it in a seasoned liquid.

clue.text: Listen to seal, another aquatic creature

indicators.note: listen to means the word for seal is heard spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: a signet is a small seal, as on a ring

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to hear a seal, and then another water animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seal' looks like the animal, which is why 'another aquatic creature' follows, but it is a SIGNET, a ring's seal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cygnet is a young swan, a bird that lives on water.
